hypothesis: If every animal with more than four feet is bloodless, and every blooded animal has no feet, two feet or four feet, then squamates (blooded) have only 0, 2 or 4 limbs and every arthropod specimen with more than four walking legs is outside the vertebrates.
pass_criterion: Both of the following. (1) In SquamBase, at least 5000 species have a limb count mapped to a number, and none of those counts is outside {0, 2, 4}. (2) In the arthropod feet dataset, at least 30 specimens have a walking-leg count strictly greater than 4, and none of those specimens is coded in a vertebrate class, phylum or order. Mammals, birds, amphibians and fishes are outside these two files and do not have to be present for a pass; their absence is a coverage caveat, not a fail.
fail_criterion: Any mapped squamate limb count is outside {0, 2, 4}, or any specimen with more than four walking legs is coded as a vertebrate. If either file cannot be retrieved, or fewer than 5000 squamates map, or fewer than 30 many-legged arthropod specimens are present, and no counterexample has already been found, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable or underpowered as appropriate. Unmapped limb strings that are more than 1% of SquamBase rows and that do not themselves state a count outside {0, 2, 4} make the verdict inconclusive with reason other, unless a mapped counterexample is already present, in which case the verdict is refutes.
interpretation: Scope maps 'blooded' to vertebrates and 'bloodless' to invertebrates. 'Feet' are paired locomotory limbs or walking legs, not digits. SquamBase categories follow Meiri's codebook: a numeric cell is that count; 'limbless' or 'absent' or 'none' maps to 0; 'forelimb only', 'hindlimb only', 'front only', 'hind only' or 'one pair' maps to 2; 'fully limbed', 'four', 'both pairs' or 'reduced' (short limbs, not an extra pair) maps to 4. A tiny vestige that the dataset itself calls limbless stays 0. Digit counts are ignored. Vertebrate coding in the arthropod file is a taxonomic field containing Vertebrata, Mammalia, Aves, Reptilia, Amphibia, Actinopterygii, Chondrichthyes, or an order in {Primates, Carnivora, Rodentia, Cetacea, Artiodactyla, Perissodactyla, Chiroptera, Squamata, Testudines, Crocodylia, Anura, Caudata, Gymnophiona, Perciformes, Cypriniformes, Siluriformes, Salmoniformes, Squaliformes, Rajiformes}.

test_contract.expected_observation: Every coded squamate has 0, 2 or 4 limbs, and every arthropod specimen with more than four walking legs is non-vertebrate.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: A squamate with a limb count other than 0, 2 or 4, or a vertebrate specimen with more than four walking legs.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Species- or specimen-level public tables that state a limb or walking-leg count and a taxon name, assembled independently of this claim, with a licence that permits download. The squamate table must cover snakes and lizards, not a single genus. The many-legged table must state walking-leg counts rather than a presence/absence of limbs.
test_contract.inference_method: Map each row to a limb count with the codebook above. A universal is refuted by one counterexample. A pass requires both sample-size floors and zero counterexamples. No phylogenetic model.

datasets.name: SquamBase 1.0 – a dataset of squamate species traits
datasets.role: limb category for each squamate species

datasets.name: Data from: Which arthropods have feet and why? Addressing an argument for aquatic fossil scorpions
datasets.role: walking-leg count and taxonomic class or order for each specimen

method: Each Dryad file was retrieved by solving the Anubis fast challenge and following the redirect to the object store. SquamBase Limbs values were mapped with the pre-registered codebook: a leading integer is that count, limbless is 0, forelimbs-only or hindlimbs-only is 2, and reduced or four well-developed limbs is 4. Arthropod rows with Leg count greater than 4 were checked for a vertebrate class or order from the pre-registered list.

measured.unit: counterexamples (squamate limb counts outside {0, 2, 4}, plus many-legged specimens coded vertebrate)
measured.uncertainty: category strings mapped with the pre-registered codebook; leading integer wins when the cell starts with a digit

caveats: Mammals, birds, amphibians and fishes are not in these two files. The pre-registration treats that absence as coverage, not as a failure.
SquamBase 'reduced' is mapped to 4 because the codebook says reduced means short limbs, not an extra pair. Digit counts are not a separate column in this file.
The arthropod table is a comparative specimen sample, not a census of arthropods.
